title: Slow-Cooker Whole Chicken
subtitle: Tender whole chicken with lemon and garlic in the slow cooker
excerpt: A whole chicken cooked breast-side up in the slow cooker with lemon, garlic, and thyme until the meat pulls away from the bone. Far more tender than roasting and needs almost no attention.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cooking a whole chicken in a slow cooker produces extraordinarily moist meat because the chicken essentially steams in its own juices. There is no crispy skin: if you want that, blast the cooked chicken under a hot grill for 5 minutes after it comes out of the slow cooker. The cooking liquid becomes an instant stock that can be used to make gravy or stored in the fridge for soup.

recipeTools.notes: Must be at least 5 litres to fit a 1.6 kg chicken.

content.text: The chicken sits breast-side up in the slow cooker. Crumple foil balls to rest the bird on so it is not sitting directly in liquid, which steams rather than slow-cooks the underside. The liquid level should come no higher than the bottom of the chicken. Check the internal temperature at the thigh joint: 75 C is safe.
Scrunch 3 to 4 balls of foil and place them in the bottom of the slow cooker insert. Rub the chicken all over with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon halves, garlic cloves, and thyme sprigs. Sit the chicken breast-side up on the foil balls.
Cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours or HIGH for 4 to 5 hours. The chicken is ready when the juices run clear at the thigh joint and the meat pulls away from the bone easily.
For crisper skin, transfer the cooked chicken to a roasting tin and place under a hot grill for 5 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before carving. Strain the cooking juices for gravy or soup stock.
